findings.title: Hotkey listener calls Tk from the Win32 worker thread
findings.impact: A hotkey or registration-error delivery can raise RuntimeError when Tk is not processing its event loop, terminating GlobalHotkeys._run and leaving every game-focus shortcut silent for the rest of the process.
findings.fix: Bind RegisterHotKey to a native message-only window owned by the Tk thread and enqueue callbacks through TkEventDispatcher without calling Tk from a worker.

evidence.detail: Python 3.14.5 repro: worker root.after before mainloop raised RuntimeError: main thread is not in main loop after 1.007 seconds; fake WM_HOTKEY repro stopped GetMessageW after one message.
fa1899cf^ and HEAD GlobalHotkeys are byte-identical, proving a latent pre-existing path rather than a changed RegisterHotKey implementation.
The outer message-loop handler catches only OSError and AttributeError, so RuntimeError escapes; current PITFALLS already describes this failure.

findings.resolution_note: Replaced worker GetMessage/root.after path with a Tk-owner message-only HWND and TkEventDispatcher delivery; 38 focused tests and real Win32 synthetic F6 smoke passed.

findings.title: Unexpected broker exit leaves the App stuck in connecting state
findings.impact: If the elevated broker connects and then exits before sending READY, ReadFile returns ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE. The client suppresses that error while not stopping, so the App never starts local fallback and keeps showing that the protected broker is connecting.
findings.fix: Treat every pipe read failure while _stopping is false as a broker failure, dispatch the visible fallback, and add a regression test for a broken pipe before READY.

evidence.detail: The expected shutdown path sets _stopping before signaling the stop event, so ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE while _stopping is false is unexpected and must not be suppressed.
Ruff and pytest pass, confirming this lifecycle branch is not covered by the existing suite.

findings.resolution_note: Pipe read failures now dispatch the visible fallback whenever the App is not stopping; tests/test_hotkey_broker.py broken-pipe regression passes.

findings.title: Broker registration failures clear the persistent recovery action
findings.impact: When one or more configured keys are already reserved, the broker reports those failures but runtime services clear the persistent notice before showing a one-time modal. This violates ELEV-07 and leaves the user without the required visible retry path after dismissing the dialog.
findings.fix: Keep the auxiliary notice row visible with a concise failed-key explanation and retry action whenever failed_keys is non-empty; clear it only after a fully successful READY frame.

evidence.detail: The handler unconditionally clears the notice before branching on failed_keys.
The accepted startup-elevation spec ELEV-07 requires a persistent explanation and retry action for registration failure.

findings.resolution_note: Failed READY frames now preserve a retry notice naming the conflicting keys; focused runtime-services tests pass.

findings.title: Broker installer trusts any pre-existing Program Files directory ACL
findings.impact: If the fixed HotkeyBroker directory already exists with a permissive DACL, create_dir_all preserves it and the installed elevated broker remains replaceable by a standard user. Because runtime currently accepts any Windows-trusted Authenticode signer, a user-writable directory would weaken the intended fixed-binary UAC boundary.
findings.fix: Apply an explicit protected DACL granting full control only to SYSTEM and Administrators and read/execute to Builtin Users on both the install directory and final broker file; fail installation if either ACL operation fails.

evidence.detail: The installer creates or reuses the directory and writes the broker without any security descriptor or ACL verification.
ELEV-03 requires administrator-only write ACLs; the current Rust build passes because no test asserts the installed DACL.

findings.resolution_note: Installer now applies a protected DACL to both the fixed Program Files directory and final broker; dev native build and startup-elevation contract tests pass.

findings.title: Mutable adjacent checksum authenticates the elevated broker
findings.impact: A same-user writer to the supported portable App directory can replace BomanaHotkeyBroker.exe and its checksum; if the user then enables administrator hotkeys and approves UAC, the replacement executes as administrator.
findings.fix: Do not offer runas from a user-writable App package. Require an OS-protected or Authenticode-verified broker boundary, or explicitly disable privileged hotkeys when no independent trust anchor is available.

evidence.detail: A temporary attacker-controlled BomanaHotkeyBroker.exe plus its matching adjacent sidecar made verify_bundled_broker() return True.
hotkey_broker.py passes the accepted path to ShellExecuteExW with lpVerb=runas; build_portable.py packages the EXE and checksum together.

launcher.pyw requires the install root to be writable and recommends a Desktop or Downloads Bomana directory; ADR 0003 acknowledges the user-writable package is weaker than Program Files plus Authenticode.
uv focused broker/elevation/build tests: 60 passed; existing tests pin matching-pair behavior but do not provide an independent trust anchor.

### 2026-07-10 — A clamped glide proxy can make every weapon the same

Symptom: all 44 generated glide records return the same height-proportional envelope, so GBU-39 and GBU-53 differ in the catalog but not in the solver.
Root cause: every real `0.08 * wingAreaMult / CxK` value fell below the hardcoded 1.5 floor, while mass, caliber, and `dragCx` never entered that path; the available fields also do not establish lift-curve or induced-drag coefficients for a defensible replacement L/D.
Spec: `docs/specs/weapon-fire-control.md` `WFC-07`, `WFC-10`, `WFC-13` (Draft 2026-07).
Pin: `tests/test_weapon_solver.py` requires glide cues to use the Datamine-backed gravity/drag trajectory only as a non-green guided-ballistic reference until live calibration establishes a lift model.
findings.title: Clamped glide proxy collapses distinct weapons into one false envelope
findings.impact: All 44 glide weapons could receive the same synthetic height-proportional range and a green/full-envelope claim despite lacking a calibrated lift model, misleading release decisions for realistic GBU-39/GBU-53 loadouts.
findings.fix: Remove the synthetic L/D path and expose only the Datamine-backed gravity/drag result as a neutral/yellow guided-ballistic reference until live calibration supports a lift model.

evidence.detail: The repository incident record states that all 44 generated glide records collapsed to the same floor-clamped height-proportional envelope while weapon-specific mass, caliber, and dragCx were unused.
WFC-07 and WFC-13 prohibit inferring a glide L/D envelope from wingAreaMult/CxK and prohibit presenting a ballistic reference as a green glide envelope.

findings.resolution_note: Removed the synthetic L/D proxy. Current solver emits guided-ballistic reference statuses, presenter keeps both states yellow, real-catalog GBU-39/GBU-53 probe produced distinct ranges, focused tests passed, full pytest passed 459 plus 12 subtests.

### 2026-07-10 — Modern propulsion blocks are not always a flat motor schedule

Symptom: PGM, AGM-130, ALARM, Kh-31, and YJ-91-family records can show a valid range even though their conditional ignition, airflow/Mach factors, factor-indexed impulses, or instantaneous mass changes were discarded or interpolated across a burn.
Root cause: flattening `propulsionN/impulseN` retained nominal thrust and mass but omitted `propulsionAutopilot`, `propulsionFactorN`, `factorIndex`, and discrete zero-time semantics.
Spec: `docs/specs/weapon-fire-control.md` `WFC-02`, `WFC-05`, `WFC-06`, `WFC-10` (Draft 2026-07).
Pin: `tests/test_weapon_data_extractor.py`, `tests/contracts/test_weapon_fire_control_schema.py`, and `tests/test_weapon_solver.py` retain machine-readable unsupported reasons and require runtime fail-closed behavior.
findings.title: Conditional propulsion semantics are flattened into invalid powered ranges
findings.impact: PGM, AGM-130, ALARM, Kh-31, and YJ-91-family weapons could show apparently valid ranges after conditional ignition, variable factors, indexed impulses, or instantaneous mass changes were silently discarded.
findings.fix: Audit modern propulsion structures into schema-backed reason codes with source pointers and fail closed at runtime for every unsupported record.

evidence.detail: The repository incident record identifies real PGM, AGM-130, ALARM, Kh-31, and YJ-91-family records whose propulsion semantics were lost by the flat schedule.
WFC-06 requires conditional propulsion autopilots, variable factors, factor-indexed impulses, and instantaneous mass changes to retain machine-readable reasons and fail closed.

findings.resolution_note: Schema and extractor now retain four unsupported propulsion reason codes and source pointers on exactly 26 records; every flagged real-catalog record returned insufficient_data/conditional_propulsion_unsupported in the runtime probe. Focused and full gates passed.

findings.snippet:
### 2026-07-10 — Missile `minDistance` is not an AAM engagement minimum

Symptom: an AIM-9L target at 50 m receives a green in-envelope cue because the top-level Datamine `minDistance` is 30 m, while the same record's condition-dependent guidance tables contain minimum ranges in the hundreds or thousands of meters.
Root cause: the solver treated a general top-level field as the lower edge of an AAM envelope even though 8111 does not provide the target aspect, motion, and altitude needed to select a guidance-table cell.
Spec: `docs/specs/weapon-fire-control.md` `WFC-06`, `WFC-08`, `WFC-13` (Draft 2026-07).
Pin: schema/extractor tests retain the guidance-table minima and their pointers, while `tests/test_weapon_solver.py` requires max-only neutral/yellow AAM output with unknown minimum range.
findings.title: Top-level missile minDistance is presented as an AAM engagement bound
findings.impact: An AIM-9L target at 50 m could receive a green full-envelope cue even though the available 8111 data cannot select the condition-dependent guidance minimum, overstating the validity of the engagement cue.
findings.fix: Retain guidance-table minimum evidence and pointers, but make runtime AAM output neutral/yellow maximum-only with the minimum explicitly unknown.

evidence.detail: The repository incident record reproduces the AIM-9L case: top-level minDistance is 30 m while guidance-table minimum ranges span hundreds or thousands of meters.
WFC-08 forbids using top-level minDistance as an AAM engagement bound without target aspect, motion, and altitude.

findings.resolution_note: Guidance-table minima remain provenance-backed (176 AAM records); runtime ignores top-level minDistance as a bound and emits yellow within_2d_max_only with min_range_m=0. AIM-9L real-catalog probe and focused/full tests passed.

findings.snippet:
### 2026-07-10 — Weapon launch TAS is not ground-target closing speed

Symptom: the card can show “time to estimated window” while flying 45 degrees away from the target, with at least a 41 percent geometric error before wind.
Root cause: remaining ground distance was divided by weapon launch speed, which prefers TAS, before alignment was checked.
Spec: `docs/specs/weapon-fire-control.md` `WFC-09`, `WFC-10`, `WFC-13` (Draft 2026-07).
Pin: `tests/test_weapon_scheduler.py` and `tests/test_weapon_solver.py` separate launch physics from aligned positive SOG closure and suppress the countdown while off-axis or opening.
findings.title: Ground time-to-window divides by launch TAS instead of aligned closure
findings.impact: The compact card could display a release-window countdown while the aircraft was flying away or substantially off-axis, with at least 41 percent geometric error before accounting for wind.
findings.fix: Keep TAS only for weapon launch physics; derive countdown closure from positive SOG multiplied by cosine of relative bearing and suppress it outside the alignment gate.

evidence.detail: The repository incident record documents a countdown while flying 45 degrees away and identifies TAS-before-alignment as the cause.
WFC-09 allows ground countdown only while aligned and requires positive along-target SOG closure; launch TAS must not be reused.

findings.resolution_note: Scheduler now separates launch TAS from positive aligned SOG*cos(relative) ground closure; real-path probe kept launch speed 250 m/s, produced 199.878 m/s closure at 2 degrees, and suppressed closure at 20 degrees. Focused/full tests passed.
